guide.line: She became a United States citizen in 1957, and graduated from Wellesley College with honors in political science two years later.

guide.line: She went on to earn a doctorate at Columbia University, worked for Senator Edmund Muskie and on President Carter's National Security Council, and taught at Georgetown University.

guide.line: In 1993 President Clinton made her the United States Ambassador to the United Nations.

guide.line: On 23 January 1997 she was sworn in as the sixty-fourth Secretary of State — the first woman to hold the job.
